jobs.title: Executive Director Finance
jobs.description:
A well-known national non-profit organization is seeking an Executive Director of Finance to join their organization. The Executive Vice President of Finance is responsible for the strategic oversight, integrity, and management of all financial operations of the organization. The EVP of Finance ensures financial transparency, regulatory compliance, and long-term institutional sustainability. Serving as the primary financial advisor to the President, CEO and Board of Directors, the EVP of Finance oversees budgeting, forecasting, financial reporting, audit and tax compliance, investment oversight, internal controls, and accounting operations.

Responsibilities:

Finance Leadership & Strategy
• Oversee all financial operations, including budgeting, forecasting, financial reporting, and
analysis.
• Develop and implement financial strategies aligned with the organization's mission and goals.
• Ensure compliance with all federal, state, and local financial and regulatory requirements.
• Manage the finance and accounting team, fostering a collaborative and high-performing
environment.
• Lead the annual audit process and ensure the accuracy and integrity of financial data.
• Collaborate with the CEO, President and Board of Directors on strategic financial planning and
decision-making.
• Develop and maintain strong relationships with external auditors, grantors, and funding sources.
• Provide timely and accurate financial analysis to inform strategic initiatives and operational
improvements.
• Maintain and enhance internal control policies and procedures to safeguard financial assets.
Strategic Planning & Organizational Capacity Building
• Partner with executive leadership to support organizational growth, program expansion, and
operational scaling.
• Identify opportunities for e6iciency, innovation, and improved service delivery through financial
insights.
• Lead special projects that enhance financial transparency, operational e6ectiveness, and impact.
Systems, Infrastructure & Transformation
• Lead modernization of financial systems (e.g., Financial Edge), including implementation,
integration with HRIS and grants systems, and change management.
• Design and optimize workflows across procure-to-pay, grant reporting, and financial close
processes.

Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree in finance or business administration required
MBA + CPA strongly preferred
15+ years of directly related finance experience required
5+ years’ experience in a non-profit organization required.

Job Description And Duties

Under the general direction of the Director and Chief Deputy Director of the DMHC, independently and through subordinate staff, the incumbent is responsible for planning, organizing, managing and directing the statewide litigation activities of the DMHC's Enforcement Program. This includes statewide responsibility for the Division of Prosecution, the Division of Investigation, and the Division of Legal Administration. The incumbent attends meetings, providing enforcement-related information on the DMHC and statewide policy issues. The incumbent is responsible for policy development, strategic planning, implementation, and evaluation of the operations within the Office of Enforcement.

The Deputy Director, Office of Enforcement, serves as principal advisor and litigator to the Director and Chief Deputy Director providing alternatives and recommendations regarding the enforcement program operations. The incumbent supervises attorneys, managers and support staff in the Office of Enforcement, and may personally perform the most difficult, complex and sensitive legal work of the DMHC in connection with the enforcement of the Knox-Keene Health Care Services Plan Act of 1975 (Act) administered by or affecting the department. jobs.title: Director of Partnerships
jobs.description:
Habitat Health empowers older adults to experience more good days in their homes and communities. Through the Program of All-Inclusive Care for the Elderly (PACE), we provide comprehensive medical care along with support for daily needs such as meals, transportation, and in‑home assistance. We deliver coordinated clinical and social care in our centers and directly in participants’ homes, creating a fully integrated experience that brings peace of mind and a true sense of belonging. As we expand our scalable, affordable PACE model to meet the growing and complex needs of aging populations, our mission‑driven care teams continue to help participants live well on their own terms.

Habitat Health is supported by leading healthcare organizations and investors including New Enterprise Associates, Kaiser Permanente, and Town Hall Ventures. We are entering a period of significant growth and are looking for exceptional teammates to help us scale a better model of care for older adults. To learn more, visit www.habitathealth.com.

Location:
Candidates must reside in California, Bay Area or Greater Los Angeles preferred, and willing to travel up to 25%

Role Scope
: The Director of Partnerships is a high-impact, cross-functional role at the core of Habitat’s thesis and operating model. This leader will facilitate pre-launch partner workstreams for new centers, mature our partner-facing operations, and nurture partner relationships from working team to executives.

We are looking for a strategic, dynamic leader who can drive deep operational execution and vision-setting with senior stakeholders – an individual with strong communication skills, sound judgment applied to ambiguous operational problems, and a track record of success across cross-cutting priorities and complex organizational dynamics.

Core Responsibilities & Expectations for the Role

Develop and manage partner relationships across all levels, from day-to-day operations to senior executives
Strengthen partner-facing workflows and tools to improve care delivery, patient experience, and market performance
Problem solve operational, partner-facing issues; derive systems-level insights, and design and deploy systematic solutions.
Build a scalable partnership management structure that supports new center launches and adapts across partner archetypes and markets.
Adapt Habitat’s operations to support expansion into new markets and local partner needs.
Deliver executive updates to Habitat and partner leadership, connecting internal initiatives to external commitments.
Support broader strategic initiatives across the enterprise, particularly where they impact partnerships.

Required Qualifications:

6–10+ years of experience in healthcare industry focused on strategy, operations, partnerships, business development, consulting
Experience in startup organization
Experience leading complex, cross-functional work from problem definition through implementation. 
Ability to bring structure to unclear problems, make practical tradeoffs, and drive outcomes across teams. 
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including comfort presenting to and influencing senior audiences.
Aligns with our purpose and our values, and is excited about living those out in daily practice.
Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, evolving environment with comfort navigating ambiguity, adapting quickly, and contributing to continuous improvement.
Strong learning and growth mindset, including seeking feedback, engaging in healthy debate and using data and curiosity to inform decisions.
Acts with integrity and ownership, considering the broader organizational impact, doing the right thing, and following through to deliver results.
Willingness to travel up to 25%

Nice to have:

Value based care and/or health care delivery experience

The final compensation offered will be determined based on factors including, but not limited to, the candidate's qualifications, skills, experience, education, certifications, geographical location, and business needs.

In addition, this position is eligible for a comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental, and vision insurance; paid parental leave, short- and long-term disability coverage; life insurance; flexible spending accounts; a 401(k) savings plan that includes a match; paid time off; and company paid holidays.

jobs.description:
About Us

Annie Aesthetic (“Annie”) is a private equity strategy focused on the medical aesthetics industry. Annie is a low-profile platform that is acquiring and operating best-in-class medical aesthetics businesses across the United States. We work alongside each of our clinics, providing financial and operational support to aid in their growth. We take an approach that optimizes for the best long-term outcomes for all parties - owners, employees, clients, and investors alike. We intentionally foster a performance-oriented, dynamic culture that values ownership, pragmatism, humility, and collaboration.

Role Overview

The Director of Operations will play a critical role in driving clinic performance and supporting growth initiatives. Reporting to the COO, the Director will serve as the full owner of one of our portfolio companies in the Los Angeles area — a business generating over $20 million in annual sales across five clinic locations, with plans to continue its rapid growth through de novo openings. This role offers a unique blend of strategic and operational responsibilities, ideal for a dynamic, results-oriented leader with a passion for building teams and growing businesses.

The Director will own portfolio company’s P&L and have all employees reporting up through them, including on-site Clinic Managers. Responsibilities span strategic planning, growth initiatives, operational excellence, talent development, and overall business performance.

The portfolio company is based in Los Angeles, so the candidate must live in the LA area and be able to be on-site three to four days per week. Some additional travel will be required, including team offsites. The majority of employees are most comfortable speaking in Mandarin so fluency is a requirement.

Duties and Responsibilities

Operational Leadership

Oversee clinic strategy development and subsequent execution in partnership with the executive team, clinic founder, and on-site Clinic Managers
Coach and train Clinic Managers on optimizing clinic operations and owning the P&L, KPI’s, and adherence to SOPs. Implement requisite meeting structure and ensure proper documentation / tracking is established for remote management.
Support management of the Annie Aesthetic Operations Associate assigned to each clinic. Coach and train junior members of the team on management of clinics and various internal workstreams.

Strategic Planning & Execution

For new acquisitions, lead the post-close integration, including the onboarding of clinic employees and Zenoti (EMR) implementation.
Assist with developing cross-functional project plans, Strategy decks, SOP’s, and checklists for day-to-day operations.
Use strategic frameworks and project management techniques to help guide people through uncertainty; manage multiple and potentially conflicting priorities; identify and manage complex dependencies.

Vendor Management & Compliance

Partner with Clinic Managers and the Zenoti team to troubleshoot issues and optimize our utilization of the software. Stay up-to-date with Zenoti product knowledge and proactively plan future adoption areas to streamline operations and increase revenue.
Interface with the third-party vendors for day-to-day needs of the clinic and ad-hoc items including: pharma / clinical, marketing, IT, maintenance / building management, etc.
Ensure adherence to regulatory requirements in each clinic related to business licenses and permits and clinical compliance and best practices.

Education / Experience

Bachelor’s degree required
5+ years of experience in consulting or operations management, with a focus on multi-site operations or M&A.

Skills / Abilities

Strong interpersonal skills with proven ability to build trusted relationships across all levels of the organization.
Ability to operate in fast-paced, ambiguous environments with a focus on results.
Track record of successfully managing multiple work streams and optimizing processes
Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to articulate complex concepts clearly and sensitive items with kindness
Advanced user of Excel; EMR and/or CRM experience is a plus
Technology integration experience is preferred
The Director will cover clinics in the greater Los Angeles area, so preference will be given to candidates living in the region. Relocation assistabce may be available for exceptional candidates that are not local. Note that candidates must be able to start within a month of receiving an offer.

Benefits

Competitive compensation including salary, bonus, and equity
Health reimbursement plan
401K plan
Flexible schedule

About the Greater Good Science Center

The Greater Good Science Center at UC Berkeley (GGSC) studies the psychology, sociology, and neuroscience of well-being and teaches skills that foster a thriving, resilient, and compassionate society. Over more than two decades, the GGSC has provided a bridge between scientists and the public, turning research findings into practical resources that support well-being for all. Since its founding, the GGSC has explored why and how to strengthen connections within families, schools, organizations, and communities, and it has highlighted the importance of building connections across group lines, offering practical strategies for overcoming bias and prejudice, expanding one’s circle of care, and promoting belonging.

The GGSC’s organizational culture prioritizes independence, rigor, social impact, and the well-being of its members. Staff members enjoy autonomy and flexibility while working in a culture that encourages teamwork, connection, and collaboration in service of our mission. The GGSC welcomes a diversity of experiences and perspectives to inform its work and strives to operate internally by the values that drive its public-facing programs: empathy, compassion, joy, forgiveness, appreciation, and cooperation. Recognizing that the science we cover has been shaped by systemic biases and inequities, we aim to address and correct for these prejudices whenever possible—a goal on which we elaborate in our Diversity Statement.

About This Position

The Associate Director of Partnerships will play a vital role in developing and managing strategic collaborations that expand the GGSC’s reach, deepen its impact, and support sustainable revenue growth. This role will focus primarily on securing content syndication and licensing opportunities with media and professional organizations, as well as identifying corporate partnerships, particularly in health care and business, to drive meaningful change within organizations in those sectors.

The Associate Director will also support the ongoing development of our CRM system and help identify advertising or sponsorship opportunities for GGSC channels aligned with our mission.
The ideal candidate has experience in partnership development and content distribution, with a strong understanding of how to leverage collaborations for both impact and revenue growth. Candidates with a strong understanding of the health care industry and the field of organizational well-being are strongly preferred.

This is a part-time (20 hours/week) career position, eligible for UC Berkeley’s robust benefits package and remote-eligible (within the United States).

Content & Distribution Partnerships

Secure syndication, licensing, or distribution opportunities with media organizations and digital platforms to advance public understanding of well-being and expand the reach of GGSC content.
Establish and maintain relationships with professional associations and other networks that reach relevant practitioners—including health care, education, and business professionals—to share GGSC content aligned with their members’ needs.
Coordinate with GGSC colleagues to ensure alignment between editorial goals and media partnerships.
Ensure partnerships reflect GGSC’s values, including scientific integrity, equity, accessibility, and a commitment to the public good.

Program & Event Partnerships

Identify and cultivate partnerships with organizations that could benefit from the GGSC’s services in speaking, training, or consulting, particularly in the fields of health care, education, or business.
Collaborate with the Greater Good Workplaces program director to develop resources, presentations, and proposals to engage potential corporate partners, particularly for workshops, consulting, or other services.
Identify and engage partners to sponsor, promote, and/or co-produce GGSC events and collaborate on co-branded events and content initiatives.
Identify partners who may be interested in placing ads in GGSC channels or on GGSC websites, or in sponsoring events, and monitor the performance of placements, working with the Director of Marketing and Partnerships to ensure advertising partnerships align with the GGSC’s brand values and audience interests.

5+ years of experience in content partnerships or business development, or comparable skills/experience
Experience with content licensing, syndication, and/or corporate sponsorships

The Managing Director will serve as the primary operational and strategic leader of MSHEF. Reporting to the co-Founders of the organization, this individual will be responsible for overseeing the foundation’s daily operations, driving fundraising initiatives, managing grant programs, and building strategic partnerships to amplify our mission.

The ideal candidate is organized, proactive, and execution-focused. 

This role is ideal for someone who thrives in a high-trust, fast-moving environment and knows how to bring structure, follow-through, and calm leadership to a growing organization. The Managing Director will help turn priorities into action, keep important relationships moving, improve internal workflows, and build the systems that make fundraising, communications, board support, and day-to-day operations more consistent and effective.

This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who is equally comfortable managing details, coordinating across many moving parts, and steadily growing into broader organizational ownership over time.

Key Responsibilities
Operational Leadership and Execution
Translate founder priorities and organizational goals into clear action plans, timelines, and follow-through
Oversee recurring workflows and help ensure critical projects, meetings, and deliverables stay on track
Build and maintain strong internal operating rhythms across planning, execution, and accountability
Identify bottlenecks, gaps, and loose ends before they become urgent
Bring work to near-completion before review whenever possible

Systems and Workflow Management
Strengthen and manage the systems that support fundraising, grants, communications, events, and board operations
Organize files, templates, calendars, trackers, and internal processes so work is easier to manage and repeat
Improve visibility around priorities, deadlines, follow-up, and organizational progress
Help create more sustainable workflows that reduce reactive, last-minute coordination
Support use and optimization of tools such as CRM platforms, planning systems, databases, and workflow trackers

Learn founder voice, judgment, and pacing in order to support communications and decision-making effectively

Relationship Management and Follow-Through
Support and eventually help lead follow-through with donors, partners, ambassadors, speakers, board members, and other strategic contacts
Draft and coordinate thoughtful outreach, follow-up, and stewardship communications
Track important touchpoints and ensure key relationships remain warm, organized, and moving forward
Help prepare for donor, partner, and board meetings with strong briefing, coordination, and follow-up systems

Board, Communications, and Initiative Support
Coordinate board agenda preparation, meeting logistics, and leadership follow-up
Support newsletters, communications drafts, and other organizational materials for founder review
Help manage preparation for campaigns, webinars, events, and strategic initiatives
Support timeline management and cross-functional coordination for major initiatives and recurring annual workstreams

What We’re Looking For

The strongest candidate will be:

Highly organized and deeply execution-oriented
Excellent at follow-through and moving work to completion
Comfortable managing multiple priorities and shifting contexts at once
Proactive, resourceful, and able to anticipate what needs attention
Strong in written communication and sound judgment around tone, discretion, and audience
Comfortable working closely with founders in a high-context, entrepreneurial environment
Confident enough to take initiative and humble enough to learn the organization’s voice, rhythm, and nuance
Mature, trustworthy, and capable of handling sensitive information with discretion

Qualifications
3–5+ years of experience in nonprofit operations, advancement operations, chief of staff support, program operations, executive support, or a similar role in a growing organization

Experience supporting senior leaders, founders, or boards where priorities shift and context matters
Strong project management and organizational skills with close attention to detail
Excellent written and verbal communication skills
Experience with CRM systems, donor platforms, project management tools, and operational workflows

Education nonprofits

Holocaust education or museum-adjacent work
Donor stewardship and advancement support
Board support and governance preparation
Event, campaign, or grant-cycle management

What Success Looks Like in the First Year
In this role, success would look like:

Stronger systems for fundraising, grants, communications, and board support
More structured and visible donor, partner, and ambassador follow-through
Less time spent by the founders on reminders, coordination, editing, and workflow management
Increased trust in the Managing Director to independently lead selected initiatives and recurring priorities
Stronger internal capacity that positions the organization for healthier long-term growth

This role is designed for someone who can make an immediate impact through execution, systems leadership, and relationship follow-through, while also growing into broader organizational responsibility over time.

This is not a purely strategic or administrative role. The CDO will personally cultivate donor relationships, develop funding opportunities, make significant asks, build fundraising systems, and move opportunities from idea to action.

The CDO will lead major gifts, individual giving, grants and institutional giving, corporate philanthropy, and donor development and stewardship.

We are looking for a leader who creates momentum.

Key Responsibilities

Philanthropic Strategy & Leadership

Build and execute a philanthropic funding strategy aligned with OLYD's mission, programs, growth priorities, and funding needs.
Establish clear fundraising goals, priorities, pipelines, timelines, and measures of success.
Create the systems and operating rhythm to move opportunities from identification through cultivation, solicitation, closing, and stewardship.
Lead team members supporting philanthropy, grants, donor engagement, and related development activities.
Establish ownership and accountability, identify obstacles early, and drive them toward resolution.
Give leadership a clear view of pipeline health, anticipated funding, risks, opportunities, and decisions needed.

Major Gifts & Donor Development

Personally identify, cultivate, solicit, and steward major individual donors and prospects.
Build and actively manage a strong major-gift pipeline rather than relying solely on existing OLYD relationships.
Develop donor strategies based on individual interests, capacity, connection to the mission, and stage of engagement.
Make significant philanthropic asks and guide other OLYD leaders through cultivation and solicitation when their involvement will strengthen an opportunity.
Activate the networks of OLYD leaders, board members, volunteers, partners, and supporters to expand our donor community.

Grants & Institutional Giving

Maintain a prioritized pipeline and calendar of grant opportunities, applications, reports, and renewals.
Provide clear direction and accountability to OLYD's grant-writing resources.
Coordinate cross-functional grant support from OLYD team members contributing expertise alongside their primary roles.
Keep grant opportunities moving by identifying missing information, setting owners and deadlines, and resolving barriers.
Partner with Program Development, Finance, and other experts to develop compelling, accurate, fundable proposals.
Ensure applications and reports are timely and OLYD meets its commitments to funders.

External Leadership & Representation

Serve as a credible philanthropic ambassador with donors, foundations, corporate partners, community leaders, and other stakeholders.
Represent OLYD independently in donor meetings, philanthropic events, networking opportunities, and presentations.
Understand OLYD's mission, programs, impact, and direction and communicate them authentically and persuasively.
Partner with the President to align organizational strategy, external positioning, and philanthropic priorities.
Engage and prepare the President, CEO, board members, program leaders, or other representatives when their involvement will strengthen an opportunity.
Help expand OLYD's visibility and credibility within philanthropic communities and networks.

Partner across teams to ensure development materials clearly communicate OLYD's work and impact.
Build a development function that can grow with OLYD beyond individual relationships or one-time efforts.

How You'll Lead

At OLYD, leadership means more than directing others.

The CDO must be comfortable moving between strategy, leadership, and execution—whether developing a multi-year strategy, coaching a team member, reviewing the grant pipeline, resolving an obstacle, preparing another executive, or personally making the ask.

You are likely to thrive in this role if you:

Take ownership of outcomes, not simply activities.
Create clarity and momentum when the path forward is not fully defined.
Proactively identify what you need and ask for it rather than waiting for someone to check in.
Bring recommendations and solutions alongside problems.
Know when to involve others without unnecessarily handing work off.
Follow through consistently and expect the same from others.
Are comfortable holding peers and senior leaders accountable to commitments that affect development outcomes.
Balance urgency and accountability with kindness, respect, and strong relationships.
Are energized by building in an early-stage environment where roles, systems, and priorities continue to evolve.
Are adaptable and comfortable wearing multiple hats, collaborating across functions, and pitching in when your expertise can help move the organization forward.

Success developing and executing philanthropic strategies that produced measurable funding growth.

It will also mean building a disciplined, scalable development engine with qualified prospects, strong donor relationships, repeatable processes, effective systems, and a program positioned to grow alongside OLYD.

Brief Description

Position Summary:

The YMCA of Greater Houston Youth Development Director supports the work of the Y, a leading nonprofit committed to strengthening community through youth development, healthy living, and social responsibility. This position develops, organizes, and implements high-quality YMCA afterschool and day camp programs throughout Fort Bend County including, but not limited to, programs at Mustang Park, Four Corners, Barbara Jordan, Wessendorff Middle School, Jones Creek, and Camp Cloud. The Youth Development Director will create a safe and positive atmosphere that welcomes and respects all individuals while inspiring youth to discover their passions. This position will enthusiastically represent the Y by displaying a positive attitude, maintaining a high level of energy and commitment to quality throughout all aspects of the job.

This position may also support the assessment, planning, development, and implementation of future afterschool programming opportunities in the Fort Bend County where they are not currently offered. The Director must be able to build relationships with schools and community stakeholders, support program startup activities, and assume operational oversight of new afterschool sites as they are established.

The Fort Bend Youth Development Director builds and maintains strong relationships with families, schools, community partners and YMCA centers through positive proactive communication. In this role, the Director ensures program quality and compliance by continuous improvement by implementing curriculum to meet licensing standards and improve quality through program evaluation and assessment. Additionally, The Youth Development Director will recruit, hire, train and onboard YMCA site leads and counselors to deliver high-quality programs while maintaining fiduciary responsibility and oversight.

Essential Functions:

Program Quality: Provides oversight and coordinates high-quality youth development programs in afterschool and outdoor day camp setting for assigned location(s), in adherence to Y program model, curriculum and quality standards. Ensure campgrounds are safe, engaging. Maintains professional and technical knowledge by attending the American Camp Association (ACA) standards training at least once every 2 years
Program Compliance: Assures compliance with state and local regulations as they relate to program areas. Ensuring that YMCA program standards are met and risk management policies are followed.
Program Planning & Innovation: Assist staff in planning, organizing, and implementing age-appropriate/developmentally appropriate program activities for afterschool programs and outdoor day camp. Fosters innovation by recognizing and sharing new and relevant ideas. Demonstrates courageous and intelligent risk taking.
Program Expansion & Development: Identifies opportunities for growth and expansion of youth development programming in the Fort Bound community. Assists with evaluating community needs, developing partnerships with schools and community organizations, supporting grant and funding objectives, and preparing for the launch and operation of new afterschool program sites as assigned.
Staff Development: Recruits, hires, trains required program staff required to meet DFPS minimum licensing standards and Y staffing ratios. Reviews and evaluates staff performance and develops strategies to motivate staff to achieve program goals.
Fiscal Management: Adheres to responsible fiscal stewardship, including managing all accounts receivable and accounts payable related to site budgets. Manage payroll related transactions and monitors for accuracy and completion. Ensures program operates within budget and meets fiscal goals through forecasting and budget monitoring.
Marketing & Promotion: Implements marketing strategies to promote program growth and brand exposure to the targeted communities and families. Expands program within the community in accordance with strategic and operating plans. Assists in the marketing and distribution of program information.
Community Engagement: Builds and maintains relationship with families through consistent communication including parent orientations, newsletters, parent conferences and parent engagement events. Actively engages in school district and/or center-based community events to build deeper relationships and YMCA brand awareness.
Center Engagement: Actively participates in YMCA center activities, meetings, and staff training. Intentionally collaborates with center program staff. Develop and maintain good working relationships with the directors, staff, parents and families by way of open communication, positive problem solving, flexibility, and teamwork.
Relationship Building: Develops and maintains strong relationships with school administration, parent and community groups and other organizations and agencies related to assigned programs. Responds to all agencies, parents and community inquiries and complaints in a timely manner.
Program Evaluation: Collects necessary qualitative and quantitative data needed to monitor program evaluation and measure program effectiveness. Lead Youth Program Quality (YPQ) intervention process at assigned locations. Use continuous program Monitors and evaluate the effectiveness of and participation in program and make adjustments to program as needed.
Annual Campaign: Participates in the annual fundraising campaign and committees as assigned at the center and meets staff campaign goals. Supports direct staff in their participation in the Better Us annual fundraising campaign.
Project Teams: Participates in project teams related to advancing the strategic vision and goals of youth development department.
Child Abuse Prevention: Reports suspicious and inappropriate behaviors and policy violations. Follows mandated abuse and incident reporting requirements. Ensures youth are properly signed in and signed out, ensures only authorized adults are allowed in the facility, etc. Adheres to policies related to boundaries with each child.

YMCA Culture & Cause Expectations

Our mission and core values are brought to life by our culture. It’s who are, who we aspire to be and how we show up every day. We are cause-driven. We don’t just show up, we show up with purpose. As a cause driven leader you are expected to be:

Welcoming-Accept neighbors eagerly, warmly, hospitably, and as equal participants.

Nurturing-To care for, support, and help develop through encouragement.

Hopeful-Take an optimistic or positive view of future outcomes.

Determined-To devote full strength and concentrated attention to the cause.

jobs.title: Chief Operating Officer
jobs.description:
About This Role:
LEDC operates using the EOS/Traction framework, which calls for a Visionary and an Integrator working side by side to lead the organization. The Chief Executive Officer serves as LEDC’s Visionary, focused on idea generation, creative problem solving, and culture. The Chief Operating Officer serves as LEDC’s Integrator, responsible for the operational execution of that vision, holding the leadership team accountable, resolving cross-departmental issues, and ensuring Human Resources, Operations, Finance, and the organization’s evaluation/impact function work in a coordinated way toward shared goals.

Position Summary:
The Chief Operating Officer (COO) is a senior leadership position responsible for the day-to-day operational execution of LEDC’s strategy. Reporting directly to the CEO, the COO oversees Human Resources, Operations, Finance, and the Impact Consultant, translating the CEO's vision and the Board-approved strategic plan into coordinated, accountable execution across departments.

The COO also represents LEDC externally in select capital, funder, and partnership relationships, particularly those tied to financial sustainability and the growth of LEDC’s lending capital base.
 Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

Strategic & Organizational Leadership
Serve as LEDC’s Integrator: run the organization’s leadership team meetings, hold department heads accountable to their priorities and performance metrics, and ensure organization-wide execution stays on track.
Translate the Board-approved strategic plan into department-level goals, and monitor execution against them.
Coordinate with CEO and program directors on staffing, operating costs, budgets, resource allocation, and feasibility of new initiatives.
Support CEO and Chief of Development by providing expertise to external relationships as needed, including maintaining relationships with banks, the CDFI Fund, and impact investors to help raise debt capital and credit facilities that fund LEDC’s loan portfolio.
Build and maintain relationships with relevant government agency partners as needed to support program and funding relationships.

Operations, Finance, & HR Leadership
Refine and design internal operating policies, policies, facilities, and administrative infrastructure to promote efficiency, accountability, and cross-functional collaboration.
Oversee Human Resources, including talent strategy, compensation structure, policies, hiring, and staff performance reviews and development systems. An integral part of overseeing HR will include benefits analysis on a yearly basis.
Oversee Operations, including facilities across LEDC’s DC, Arlington, Baltimore, White Oak offices, IT/systems infrastructure, vendor contracts, and insurance.
Oversee the Finance department’s strategic direction in partnership with the Director of Finance, including budget and audit cadence, without displacing the Director of Finance’s day-to-day leadership of the Finance team.
Oversee work of organizational consultants implementing process and systems improvements (e.g. new database builds, impact evaluation, Traction implementation).

Processes, Systems, & Accountability
Identify and manage organizational risk, including compliance, data security, and operational risk beyond purely financial matters.
Evaluate and pilot new tools (e.g., AI implementation), new processes (e.g. impact evaluation, market analysis, earned revenue), and manage related policy and training.
Own the EOS model implementation across teams: scorecards, rocks, quarterly reviews.

Compliance & Risk Management
Ensure LEDC maintains compliance with the financial covenants tied to its CDFI lending capital raise, working closely with the Director of Lending to structure, monitor, and report on covenant compliance to lenders and investors.
Partner closely with the Director of Lending to ensure LEDC maintains sufficient liquidity to support and grow its loan portfolio, coordinating capital planning between Finance and Lending.
Lead enterprise risk management across the organization: identify, assess, and prioritize strategic, operational, financial, compliance, and reputational risks, and develop mitigation, contingency, and business continuity plans appropriate to LEDC’s size, mission, and risk exposure.
Champion data security, cybersecurity, and privacy practices across the organization, and ensure LEDC carries adequate insurance coverage to protect its people, assets, and mission.
Provide regular risk assessments and updates to the CEO and Board of Directors to support informed governance and oversight.

Specific duties may vary based on program needs, funding requirements, and operational priorities. As the role evolves, additional responsibilities may be assigned.

Required Qualifications:
We recognize that candidates may meet these qualifications in different ways and encourage individuals with a passion for community-centered work to apply, even if their experience does not align perfectly with every item listed.
 5+ years of leadership experience in nonprofit operations, program management, or related field.
Demonstrated experience diagnosing organizational problems and translating them into process or systems fixes.
Demonstrated strategic thinking and change leadership; designing and implementing program strategies, leading organizational transformation, and maintaining focus amid complexity and shifting conditions.
Experience with organizational operations, finance, and/or HR management.
Strong background in data systems, reporting, and impact measurement, with an ability to champion quality programs, utilize data for evaluation and continuous improvement, and drive accountability for results.
Exceptional communication and cross-functional leadership skills, including influence without direct authority.

Preferred Qualifications:
Experience with Traction/EOS or similar operating systems, Airtable or comparable database platforms, and CDFI/nonprofit program environments preferred.
Bilingual in English and Spanish, with professional proficiency in reading, writing, and verbal communication in Spanish.
Background in Finance, including both external audits, federal grants management, accounting regulations, and in-house financial management experience a plus.
Experience in a CDFI, community development finance, or other mission-driven lending organization strongly preferred, and/or Business or accounting degree or CPA a plus.

Work Environment & Schedule:
Work Environment: This job operates in a professional office environment. This role routinely uses standard office equipment, such as computers, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets and scanners.
The office environment is generally climate-controlled; however, temperatures may vary, and some individuals may find it too warm or too cool at times.
Hybrid Work Model: LEDC maintains a hybrid workplace model. In-office schedules vary by team, but all staff are expected to be able to report to the office any day of the week, as needed.
Schedule: Typical office hours are 9am-5pm, however the finalized schedule is approved by the CEO. This is a full-time, exempt position which typically requires 40 hours per week. Evening or weekend work and travel outside of normal hours should be expected periodically.
Travel: This role requires travel for meetings with funders, banks, and partners, as well as events and visits to other LEDC office locations within the DMV region and, occasionally, Puerto Rico.
Primary Reporting Location: 1401 Columbia Rd. NW, Unit C-1, Washington, DC 20009.

This is largely a sedentary role; however, some or all of the following may be required.:
Ability to remain in a stationary position for prolonged periods (e.g., sitting at a desk).
Ability to move about the office to access files, office machinery, etc.
Ability to occasionally move/lift/carry up to 10-20 pounds (e.g., office supplies, files, equipment).
Constant operation of a computer, keyboard, mouse, and other office productivity machinery, such as a calculator, copy machine and scanner.
Ability to communicate clearly and effectively in person, over the phone, and in writing.
Ability to see details at close range (within a few feet).
Ability to hear and respond to spoken communication during meetings, calls, and office interactions.
Ability to enter and move through commercial buildings, including navigating stairs, elevators, hallways, and uneven surfaces, when traveling to meetings or other office locations.

This list is not exhaustive, and other reasonable physical requirements may be assigned as needed to support the role. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of this job.

Options for employer-paid healthcare, dental, vision, disability, and life insurance.
Paid sick leave, vacation, and personal days.
Additional benefits and resources to support employee wellbeing.

jobs.description:
TYLin
is a globally recognized, full-service infrastructure consulting firm committed to providing innovative, cost-effective, constructible designs for the global infrastructure market. With over 3,000 employees throughout the Americas, Asia, and Europe, the firm provides support on projects of varying size and complexity. Together, we enhance conventional designs with smarter, more resilient systems. We provide people with better mobility. We steward precious resources by finding more sustainable solutions.

Job Summary

At TYLin, we are shaping the future of aviation infrastructure by delivering some of the world's most complex and transformative airport programs. As passenger expectations evolve and airports continue to expand into sophisticated transportation hubs, we are seeking an accomplished Program Director – Airport Terminals to provide strategic leadership on major terminal redevelopment projects.

This is a career-defining opportunity to join one of the industry's leading aviation teams and help deliver iconic airport facilities that will serve millions of passengers for decades to come.

We are seeking a nationally or internationally recognized leader with deep experience delivering large-scale airport terminal projects from planning and design through construction support. If you have successfully led multidisciplinary teams on flagship terminal developments and enjoy working with owners, executive stakeholders, and technical experts, we want to hear from you.

Relocation assistance is available for exceptional candidates currently residing elsewhere in the United States.

Responsibilities & Qualifications

The Opportunity

As Program Manager Lead, you will serve as the senior leader responsible for guiding the planning, design, and delivery of major airport terminal programs. You will provide strategic direction to multidisciplinary teams while acting as a trusted advisor to airport authorities, design partners, contractors, and executive stakeholders.

You will oversee complex projects involving terminal redevelopment, expansions, passenger processing facilities, landside interfaces, support buildings, and associated infrastructure.

This role requires exceptional leadership, technical credibility, commercial awareness, and the ability to successfully navigate the complexities of multi-billion-dollar capital programs.

Responsibilities

Lead the planning and delivery of major airport terminal design and redevelopment programs.
Serve as the primary executive interface with airport owners, program management teams, and key stakeholders.
Direct multidisciplinary teams consisting of architects, engineers, planners, and specialty consultants.
Develop program execution strategies that support cost, schedule, quality, and risk objectives.
Provide executive oversight throughout planning, design, procurement, and construction support phases.
Manage project governance, reporting, and executive communications.
Guide technical decision-making while balancing operational, commercial, and passenger experience priorities.
Coordinate with design-build teams, CMAR teams, joint ventures, and alternative delivery partners.
Identify project risks and develop mitigation strategies for large, complex programs.
Mentor and develop project managers and technical leaders across the aviation practice.
Support business development activities, client relationship management, and strategic growth initiatives.

Qualifications

Required

Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Architecture, Planning, or a related discipline.
15+ years of progressive experience delivering major aviation infrastructure projects.
Demonstrated leadership of large airport terminal design programs within the United States or internationally.
Experience managing complex, multidisciplinary consultant teams.
Proven ability to oversee large capital programs with multiple concurrent workstreams.
Strong executive presence with exceptional communication and stakeholder management skills.
Experience working directly with airport authorities, owners, executive leadership, and major program stakeholders.
Thorough understanding of airport planning, terminal design, passenger experience, and operational requirements.
Experience with alternative delivery methods including Design-Build, Progressive Design-Build, CMAR, or Public-Private Partnerships (P3).
Ability to lead high-performing teams in a collaborative environment.

Preferred

Professional Engineer (PE), Registered Architect (RA), or AICP certification.
Experience delivering projects for major international hub airports.
Experience on terminal redevelopment programs valued in the hundreds of millions or billions of dollars.
Existing relationships with major North American airport owners and aviation industry stakeholders.
Experience leading geographically dispersed project teams.

Ideal Background

We welcome candidates from a variety of professional disciplines, including:

Civil Engineering
Structural Engineering
Mechanical or Electrical Engineering
Architecture
Aviation Planning
Airport Program Management

Most importantly, you will have successfully led the delivery of significant airport terminal projects and possess the leadership capabilities to guide multidisciplinary teams on complex aviation programs.

Why TYLin?

At TYLin, you'll join one of the world's premier aviation consulting teams, partnering with airport owners to deliver transformational infrastructure that enhances mobility, sustainability, and the passenger experience.

We offer:

Opportunity to lead nationally significant airport terminal programs.
Collaborative environment with internationally recognized aviation experts.
Career growth within a global infrastructure consulting firm.
Competitive compensation and comprehensive benefits.
Relocation assistance for qualified candidates moving to the New York metropolitan area.
The opportunity to leave a lasting legacy on some of the most iconic airport developments in North America.

Join Us

If you have built your career leading the delivery of major airport terminals and are looking for your next executive leadership opportunity, we encourage you to apply.

Bring your expertise, vision, and leadership to TYLin and help redefine the future of airport infrastructure.

Additional Information

TYLin is committed to pay equity. As part of that commitment, we have provided the base compensation range of $200,000 - $290,000 annually for this position and local market. We recognize that each candidate brings a unique set of skills, experience, education and competencies to the table that will be reflected in our offer. TYLin is proud to offer exciting career development opportunities.

TYLin
offers a comprehensive total rewards package. Our benefits may include extensive medical, disability and life insurance coverage, continuing education benefits, paid time off, employee assistance program and a retirement savings plan with company matching contributions.

We encourage all candidates to explore our total rewards offering.

Collaboration, mission-driven focus, discipline, and leadership skills developed through military service benefit us all. Whether you are a Veteran, Guardsman or Reservist, a Military Spouse or you are planning to transition to civilian life in the near future, we welcome and value your application.

TYLin
is an equal opportunity employer, and we prohibit discrimination and harassment of any type as protected by federal, provincial, state or local laws. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. The company and its employees are required to comply with all local health authority, legal or lawful client requirements.

About the Greater Good Science Center

The Greater Good Science Center at UC Berkeley (GGSC) studies the psychology, sociology, and neuroscience of well-being and teaches skills that foster a thriving, resilient, and compassionate society. Over more than two decades, the GGSC has provided a bridge between scientists and the public, turning research findings into practical resources that support well-being for all. Since its founding, the GGSC has explored why and how to strengthen connections within families, schools, organizations, and communities, and it has highlighted the importance of building connections across group lines, offering practical strategies for overcoming bias and prejudice, expanding one’s circle of care, and promoting belonging.

The GGSC’s organizational culture prioritizes independence, rigor, social impact, and the well-being of its members. Staff members enjoy autonomy and flexibility while working in a culture that encourages teamwork, connection, and collaboration in service of our mission. The GGSC welcomes a diversity of experiences and perspectives to inform its work and strives to operate internally by the values that drive its public-facing programs: empathy, compassion, joy, forgiveness, appreciation, and cooperation. Recognizing that the science we cover has been shaped by systemic biases and inequities, we aim to address and correct for these prejudices whenever possible—a goal on which we elaborate in our Diversity Statement.

About This Position

The Associate Director of Partnerships will play a vital role in developing and managing strategic collaborations that expand the GGSC’s reach, deepen its impact, and support sustainable revenue growth. This role will focus primarily on securing content syndication and licensing opportunities with media and professional organizations, as well as identifying corporate partnerships, particularly in health care and business, to drive meaningful change within organizations in those sectors.

The Associate Director will also support the ongoing development of our CRM system and help identify advertising or sponsorship opportunities for GGSC channels aligned with our mission.
The ideal candidate has experience in partnership development and content distribution, with a strong understanding of how to leverage collaborations for both impact and revenue growth. Candidates with a strong understanding of the health care industry and the field of organizational well-being are strongly preferred.

This is a part-time (20 hours/week) career position, eligible for UC Berkeley’s robust benefits package and remote-eligible (within the United States).

Content & Distribution Partnerships

Secure syndication, licensing, or distribution opportunities with media organizations and digital platforms to advance public understanding of well-being and expand the reach of GGSC content.
Establish and maintain relationships with professional associations and other networks that reach relevant practitioners—including health care, education, and business professionals—to share GGSC content aligned with their members’ needs.
Coordinate with GGSC colleagues to ensure alignment between editorial goals and media partnerships.
Ensure partnerships reflect GGSC’s values, including scientific integrity, equity, accessibility, and a commitment to the public good.

Program & Event Partnerships

Identify and cultivate partnerships with organizations that could benefit from the GGSC’s services in speaking, training, or consulting, particularly in the fields of health care, education, or business.
Collaborate with the Greater Good Workplaces program director to develop resources, presentations, and proposals to engage potential corporate partners, particularly for workshops, consulting, or other services.
Identify and engage partners to sponsor, promote, and/or co-produce GGSC events and collaborate on co-branded events and content initiatives.
Identify partners who may be interested in placing ads in GGSC channels or on GGSC websites, or in sponsoring events, and monitor the performance of placements, working with the Director of Marketing and Partnerships to ensure advertising partnerships align with the GGSC’s brand values and audience interests.

Partnership Research & Maintenance

Maintain and improve comprehensive partnership tracking in a CRM system, ensuring data is accurate and up to date, with support from a student assistant.

Coordinate partnership-related communications and documentation, including contracts, advertising asset approval and agreements, proposals, and reports.
Contribute to strategic planning discussions and collaborate cross-functionally to support organizational goals.
Identify opportunities to package the GGSC’s existing articles, practices, and other resources into digital or print products co-branded with other organizations, including health care and mental health professionals, and assess opportunities to monetize GGSC content and materials through licensing and sales.

Main Qualifications*

5+ years of experience in content partnerships or business development, or comparable skills/experience
Experience with content licensing, syndication, and/or corporate sponsorships

Demonstrated alignment with the Greater Good Science Center’s mission

The Schenectady Greenmarket is a regional farmers market that brings together vendors, shoppers, musicians, and community members in a vibrant, inclusive setting. The market plays a key role in Schenectady’s cultural landscape by connecting farms and urban neighborhoods to help build a resilient, equitable, and sustainable local food system. Schenectady Greenmarket is committed to maintaining a diverse marketplace that is accessible to all, with vendors who reflect the cultures and experiences of the surrounding communities. The organization collaborates with community partners to promote education about farmers, healthy food, and food access, fostering deeper connections between local agriculture and residents. Team members join a mission-driven environment dedicated to community engagement and food justice.

Role Overview (Full Time)

The Executive Director (ED) serves as the chief administrator of the Schenectady Greenmarket. This leadership role is responsible for the organization's strategic direction, financial health, and long-term sustainability.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership & Board Relations

●     Implement and coordinate Board policies and actions to ensure long-term organizational effectiveness.
●     Collaborate with the Board Chair to develop meeting agendas and set organizational priorities and goals.
●     Prepare regular written repots to the Board concerning activities
●     Cultivate and maintain strategic partnerships and community collaborations that support the market's mission.
Finance & Development

●     Drive revenue growth through diversified fundraising activities, grant applications, and sponsorship outreach.
●     Manage donor relations, ensuring all sponsors and contributors are appropriately recognized.
●     Oversee financial reporting in collaboration with the Treasurer and accountants, including annual budget reviews and weekly deposits.
●     Coordinate fundraising events with the support of staff, volunteers, and the Board.
Operations & Human Resources

●     Supervise, mentor, and train market staff, including managing performance evaluations, HR policies, and payroll.
●     Oversee market software and processes (MMM, Donor Snap) and provide operational coverage for the Market Manager as needed.
●     Develop and manage volunteer recruitment, training, and recognition programs.
●     Manage contracts, permits, and MOUs with the City of Schenectady, landlords, and partner organizations.
●     Resolve complex vendor issues and coordinate with promotions firms for market events and announcements.

Other Duties—as assigned
Preferred Qualifications

●     Proven success in community outreach and an understanding of food system inequalities.
●     Experience in writing grant proposals and doing follow-up grant reporting
●     Strong leadership skills with experience managing remote teams and volunteers.
●     Excellent organizational and communication skills, both written and verbal.
●     Ability to work collaboratively with diverse populations across race, gender, religion, and orientation.
●     Proficiency in Microsoft Office, Google Workspace, and standard management software.
●     Flexibility to work varied schedules, including occasional Sundays and outdoor market conditions.
●     Fluency in other languages (especially Spanish) and familiarity with farming practices are a plus.

The Role
The Managing Director will serve as the primary operational and strategic leader of MSHEF. Reporting to the co-Founders of the organization, this individual will be responsible for overseeing the foundation’s daily operations, driving fundraising initiatives, managing grant programs, and building strategic partnerships to amplify our mission.

The ideal candidate is organized, proactive, and execution-focused. 

This role is ideal for someone who thrives in a high-trust, fast-moving environment and knows how to bring structure, follow-through, and calm leadership to a growing organization. The Managing Director will help turn priorities into action, keep important relationships moving, improve internal workflows, and build the systems that make fundraising, communications, board support, and day-to-day operations more consistent and effective.

This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who is equally comfortable managing details, coordinating across many moving parts, and steadily growing into broader organizational ownership over time.

Key Responsibilities
Operational Leadership and Execution
Translate founder priorities and organizational goals into clear action plans, timelines, and follow-through
Oversee recurring workflows and help ensure critical projects, meetings, and deliverables stay on track
Build and maintain strong internal operating rhythms across planning, execution, and accountability
Identify bottlenecks, gaps, and loose ends before they become urgent
Bring work to near-completion before review whenever possible

Systems and Workflow Management
Strengthen and manage the systems that support fundraising, grants, communications, events, and board operations
Organize files, templates, calendars, trackers, and internal processes so work is easier to manage and repeat
Improve visibility around priorities, deadlines, follow-up, and organizational progress
Help create more sustainable workflows that reduce reactive, last-minute coordination
Support use and optimization of tools such as CRM platforms, planning systems, databases, and workflow trackers

Founder and Leadership Support
Serve as a trusted thought partner and execution partner to the founders
Help prepare materials, updates, talking points, and planning support for leadership conversations and meetings
Reduce the founders’ administrative and coordination burden by taking ownership of routine follow-up, reminders, and process management
Learn founder voice, judgment, and pacing in order to support communications and decision-making effectively

Relationship Management and Follow-Through
Support and eventually help lead follow-through with donors, partners, ambassadors, speakers, board members, and other strategic contacts
Draft and coordinate thoughtful outreach, follow-up, and stewardship communications
Track important touchpoints and ensure key relationships remain warm, organized, and moving forward
Help prepare for donor, partner, and board meetings with strong briefing, coordination, and follow-up systems

Board, Communications, and Initiative Support
Coordinate board agenda preparation, meeting logistics, and leadership follow-up
Support newsletters, communications drafts, and other organizational materials for founder review
Help manage preparation for campaigns, webinars, events, and strategic initiatives
Support timeline management and cross-functional coordination for major initiatives and recurring annual workstreams

What We’re Looking For

The strongest candidate will be:

Highly organized and deeply execution-oriented
Excellent at follow-through and moving work to completion
Comfortable managing multiple priorities and shifting contexts at once
Proactive, resourceful, and able to anticipate what needs attention
Strong in written communication and sound judgment around tone, discretion, and audience
Comfortable working closely with founders in a high-context, entrepreneurial environment
Confident enough to take initiative and humble enough to learn the organization’s voice, rhythm, and nuance
Mature, trustworthy, and capable of handling sensitive information with discretion

Qualifications
3–5+ years of experience in nonprofit operations, advancement operations, chief of staff support, program operations, executive support, or a similar role in a growing organization
Demonstrated success building order, systems, and follow-through in a fast-moving environment
Experience supporting senior leaders, founders, or boards where priorities shift and context matters
Strong project management and organizational skills with close attention to detail
Excellent written and verbal communication skills
Experience with CRM systems, donor platforms, project management tools, and operational workflows
Ability to manage ambiguity, prioritize effectively, and keep momentum across multiple workstreams
Commitment to the mission and values of MSHE Foundation

Preferred Experience
Candidates with experience in one or more of the following areas are especially encouraged to apply:

Education nonprofits
Jewish nonprofit organizations
Holocaust education or museum-adjacent work
Donor stewardship and advancement support
Board support and governance preparation
Event, campaign, or grant-cycle management

What Success Looks Like in the First Year
In this role, success would look like:

Stronger systems for fundraising, grants, communications, and board support
More structured and visible donor, partner, and ambassador follow-through
Less time spent by the founders on reminders, coordination, editing, and workflow management
Increased trust in the Managing Director to independently lead selected initiatives and recurring priorities
Stronger internal capacity that positions the organization for healthier long-term growth

Growth Opportunity
This role is designed for someone who can make an immediate impact through execution, systems leadership, and relationship follow-through, while also growing into broader organizational responsibility over time.

As trust and context build, this person may expand into deeper donor ownership, stronger board leadership support, broader management of staff and contractors, and increased ownership of planning and strategic initiative execution.

Compensation
Expected compensation for this role is in the range of $95,000–$105,000
, with the potential for performance-based bonus consideration tied to execution, stewardship, and organizational goals. Compensation will ultimately depend on experience and readiness for the scope of the role.

To Apply
Please submit your resume through Indeed and a brief video of not more than 2 minutes explaining your interest in the role and your relevant experience. Tell us why this mission is important to you. While you will still need to formally apply through Indeed, the video can be sent to info@mshefoundation.org with the subject line: FULL NAME: VIDEO SUBMISSION.

Job Summary

The Division of Research and Innovation is seeking a Frontiers of Advanced Semiconductor Technology (FAST) Engine Chief Executive Officer. This is a full-time (1.00 FTE), 12-month, professional faculty position.

The Frontiers of Advanced Semiconductor Technology (FAST) NSF Regional Innovation Engine is seeking an entrepreneurial and visionary Chief Executive Officer to lead one of the nation’s premier place-based innovation initiatives. Backed by the National Science Foundation and a coalition of more than 95 partners, FAST is advancing U.S. leadership in AI-enabled semiconductor manufacturing while driving innovation, workforce development, and economic growth across Oregon.

Reporting to the Associate Vice President for Economic Development and Industry Relations at Oregon State University and working closely with the FAST Strategic Governing Council, the CEO will lead a complex, multi-institutional organization spanning research universities, community colleges, industry, government, workforce organizations, investors, and community partners. The CEO will be responsible for achieving ambitious technical, workforce, commercialization, and regional economic development outcomes; successfully advancing the Engine through NSF stage-gate reviews; and building FAST into a nationally recognized, financially sustainable innovation enterprise.

About FAST

Frontiers of Advanced Semiconductor Technology (FAST) https://fast-engine.org/ is a National Science Foundation (NSF) designated Regional Innovation Engine https://www.nsf.gov/funding/initiatives/regional-innovation-engines/about-nsf-engines advancing U.S. leadership in semiconductor manufacturing through the development and deployment of AI-enabled Advanced Process Control (AI-APC) systems. FAST is a consortium of more than 95 industry, academic, government, workforce, and community partners aligned to catalyze innovation, workforce development, and inclusive economic growth across Oregon’s Cascade-Willamette Innovation Corridor (CWIC). FAST is one of the National Science Foundation’s Regional Innovation Engines, designed to strengthen U.S. economic competitiveness through long-term regional innovation ecosystems that integrate research, commercialization, workforce development, entrepreneurship, and industry engagement.

FAST integrates use-inspired research, translation of innovation to practice, entrepreneurship, workforce development, and regional engagement to create a globally competitive semiconductor ecosystem with national economic and security impact. The Engine is funded by NSF for up to 10 years, with substantial state, industry, and philanthropic co-investment.

Key Responsibilities

Serve as the chief executive and public face of FAST, articulating and advancing a compelling long-term vision for the Engine’s impact and sustainability.
Direct a complex statewide partnership of universities, community colleges, industry, government, workforce organizations, and investors.
Deliver measurable outcomes in semiconductor innovation, commercialization, workforce development, and regional economic competitiveness.
Lead FAST through successful NSF stage-gate reviews following the initial two-year award period by ensuring the Engine achieves its milestone-based performance objectives, demonstrates measurable commercialization and regional economic impact, and secures subsequent phases of NSF funding.
Build executive-level relationships with federal agencies, industry leaders, investors, elected officials, and academic partners.
Expand FAST’s long-term financial sustainability through strategic partnerships and diversified public and private investment.
Lead and develop FAST’s executive leadership team, providing strategic direction, performance management, and organizational leadership across a complex, multi-institutional organization.
Partner closely with FAST Directors and Co-Directors to align research, workforce, commercialization, and partnership activities in support of the Engine’s strategic goals and NSF performance milestones.
Serve as the public face and national spokesperson for FAST and Oregon’s semiconductor innovation ecosystem.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree in engineering, physical sciences, business, or a related field.
Experience in semiconductors, advanced manufacturing, AI, or closely related technology sectors.
Minimum of 10 years of senior leadership experience with demonstrated responsibility for complex, multi-stakeholder organizations or initiatives.
Proven ability to lead at the intersection of technology, industry, and economic development.
Demonstrated success securing and managing large-scale public and private funding.
Strong record of building partnerships across industry, academia, government, and communities.
Exceptional communication skills and executive presence, with a proven ability to align diverse stakeholders around shared goals.
Commitment to inclusive excellence and inclusive regional prosperity.
