Chief Development Officer

Reports to
: President, OLYD
Role Type:
Executive Leadership
Compensation:
Founding, equity-only role at this stage; compensation is expected to evolve as OLYD's funding and revenue grow.

About OLYD

Oh! Love Ya Dawn (OLYD) is a shared movement where creativity, compassion, and purpose come together.

Through the Oh! Love Ya Dawn Company, we build products, platforms, and experiences that carry meaning and connection. Through our Foundation, we turn those efforts into programs that protect and uplift children who have experienced abuse or neglect.

Together, we are creating something that proves business can have a heartbeat and that structure and humanity can grow side by side.

Role Overview

OLYD is seeking an experienced, highly proactive Chief Development Officer (CDO) to build and lead our philanthropic funding strategy while remaining deeply engaged in the work.

This is not a purely strategic or administrative role. The CDO will personally cultivate donor relationships, develop funding opportunities, make significant asks, build fundraising systems, and move opportunities from idea to action.

The CDO will lead major gifts, individual giving, grants and institutional giving, corporate philanthropy, and donor development and stewardship.

We are looking for a leader who creates momentum.

The right person will assess where we are, determine what is needed, develop a path forward, engage the right people and resources, remove barriers, and keep the work moving.

Key Responsibilities

Philanthropic Strategy & Leadership

Build and execute a philanthropic funding strategy aligned with OLYD's mission, programs, growth priorities, and funding needs.
Establish clear fundraising goals, priorities, pipelines, timelines, and measures of success.
Create the systems and operating rhythm to move opportunities from identification through cultivation, solicitation, closing, and stewardship.
Lead team members supporting philanthropy, grants, donor engagement, and related development activities.
Establish ownership and accountability, identify obstacles early, and drive them toward resolution.
Give leadership a clear view of pipeline health, anticipated funding, risks, opportunities, and decisions needed.

Major Gifts & Donor Development

Personally identify, cultivate, solicit, and steward major individual donors and prospects.
Build and actively manage a strong major-gift pipeline rather than relying solely on existing OLYD relationships.
Develop donor strategies based on individual interests, capacity, connection to the mission, and stage of engagement.
Make significant philanthropic asks and guide other OLYD leaders through cultivation and solicitation when their involvement will strengthen an opportunity.
Activate the networks of OLYD leaders, board members, volunteers, partners, and supporters to expand our donor community.
Build long-term relationships that create sustained philanthropic engagement.

Grants & Institutional Giving

Lead a proactive institutional-giving strategy across private, family, and corporate foundations and other appropriate grantmakers.
Maintain a prioritized pipeline and calendar of grant opportunities, applications, reports, and renewals.
Provide clear direction and accountability to OLYD's grant-writing resources.
Coordinate cross-functional grant support from OLYD team members contributing expertise alongside their primary roles.
Keep grant opportunities moving by identifying missing information, setting owners and deadlines, and resolving barriers.
Partner with Program Development, Finance, and other experts to develop compelling, accurate, fundable proposals.
Ensure applications and reports are timely and OLYD meets its commitments to funders.

External Leadership & Representation

Serve as a credible philanthropic ambassador with donors, foundations, corporate partners, community leaders, and other stakeholders.
Represent OLYD independently in donor meetings, philanthropic events, networking opportunities, and presentations.
Understand OLYD's mission, programs, impact, and direction and communicate them authentically and persuasively.
Partner with the President to align organizational strategy, external positioning, and philanthropic priorities.
Engage and prepare the President, CEO, board members, program leaders, or other representatives when their involvement will strengthen an opportunity.
Help expand OLYD's visibility and credibility within philanthropic communities and networks.

Development Infrastructure & Stewardship

Evaluate current development practices and establish scalable processes, tools, and systems where needed.
Build disciplined practices for prospect management, donor records, relationship tracking, stewardship, and reporting.
Establish stewardship strategies that demonstrate impact, deepen relationships, and encourage continued engagement.
Partner across teams to ensure development materials clearly communicate OLYD's work and impact.
Build a development function that can grow with OLYD beyond individual relationships or one-time efforts.

How You'll Lead

At OLYD, leadership means more than directing others.

The CDO must be comfortable moving between strategy, leadership, and execution—whether developing a multi-year strategy, coaching a team member, reviewing the grant pipeline, resolving an obstacle, preparing another executive, or personally making the ask.

You are likely to thrive in this role if you:

Take ownership of outcomes, not simply activities.
Create clarity and momentum when the path forward is not fully defined.
Proactively identify what you need and ask for it rather than waiting for someone to check in.
Bring recommendations and solutions alongside problems.
Know when to involve others without unnecessarily handing work off.
Follow through consistently and expect the same from others.
Are comfortable holding peers and senior leaders accountable to commitments that affect development outcomes.
Balance urgency and accountability with kindness, respect, and strong relationships.
Are energized by building in an early-stage environment where roles, systems, and priorities continue to evolve.
Are adaptable and comfortable wearing multiple hats, collaborating across functions, and pitching in when your expertise can help move the organization forward.
Use good judgment and take initiative—building what is needed, making the most of what exists, and moving good ideas forward without unnecessary permission while keeping the right people informed and engaged.
Believe that being an executive leader and being willing to do the work are not mutually exclusive.

What You Bring

Required

Significant experience in nonprofit development, philanthropy, or institutional advancement, with increasing responsibility for strategy and results.
Success developing and executing philanthropic strategies that produced measurable funding growth.
A strong major-gift cultivation and solicitation record, including personally making significant donor asks.
Experience building and managing donor or prospect pipelines from identification through stewardship.
Institutional-giving and grant-development knowledge sufficient to lead and hold a grants function accountable.
Ability to build relationships with high-net-worth individuals, foundations, corporate philanthropic partners, and other funders.
Experience leading people and cross-functional initiatives through influence, accountability, and collaboration.
Strong executive presence and the ability to represent OLYD credibly with external audiences.
Exceptional written and verbal communication skills.
Self-direction, resourcefulness, follow-through, and comfort in a growing organization where every system may not already exist.
Experience building or significantly scaling a philanthropic development function, including creating prospect pipelines, processes, systems, relationships, and operating practices where significant infrastructure was needed.

Preferred

Experience with organizations serving children, youth, families, foster care, education, mentorship, or related social-impact areas.
Experience engaging founders, executives, boards, and volunteer leaders in donor cultivation and solicitation.
Experience developing corporate philanthropy or strategic philanthropic partnerships.
Experience establishing development systems, metrics, and reporting practices.

What Success Looks Like

Success will be reflected in consistent fundraising activity, a growing and qualified donor pipeline, grants and proposals moving forward, stronger philanthropic relationships, increased funding, and a development function that knows what it is doing next and why.

It will also mean building a disciplined, scalable development engine with qualified prospects, strong donor relationships, repeatable processes, effective systems, and a program positioned to grow alongside OLYD.

The CDO will help OLYD build a deliberate, relationship-driven development program capable of supporting our mission for the long term.

Equal Opportunity

Position Summary:

The YMCA of Greater Houston Youth Development Director supports the work of the Y, a leading nonprofit committed to strengthening community through youth development, healthy living, and social responsibility. This position develops, organizes, and implements high-quality YMCA afterschool and day camp programs throughout Fort Bend County including, but not limited to, programs at Mustang Park, Four Corners, Barbara Jordan, Wessendorff Middle School, Jones Creek, and Camp Cloud. The Youth Development Director will create a safe and positive atmosphere that welcomes and respects all individuals while inspiring youth to discover their passions. This position will enthusiastically represent the Y by displaying a positive attitude, maintaining a high level of energy and commitment to quality throughout all aspects of the job.

This position may also support the assessment, planning, development, and implementation of future afterschool programming opportunities in the Fort Bend County where they are not currently offered. The Director must be able to build relationships with schools and community stakeholders, support program startup activities, and assume operational oversight of new afterschool sites as they are established.

The Fort Bend Youth Development Director builds and maintains strong relationships with families, schools, community partners and YMCA centers through positive proactive communication. Program Compliance: Assures compliance with state and local regulations as they relate to program areas. Ensuring that YMCA program standards are met and risk management policies are followed.

Ensures youth are properly signed in and signed out, ensures only authorized adults are allowed in the facility, etc. Adheres to policies related to boundaries with each child.

Our mission and core values are brought to life by our culture. It’s who are, who we aspire to be and how we show up every day. We are cause-driven. We don’t just show up, we show up with purpose. As a cause driven leader you are expected to be:

Welcoming-Accept neighbors eagerly, warmly, hospitably, and as equal participants.

Nurturing-To care for, support, and help develop through encouragement.

Hopeful-Take an optimistic or positive view of future outcomes.

Determined-To devote full strength and concentrated attention to the cause.

About This Role:
LEDC operates using the EOS/Traction framework, which calls for a Visionary and an Integrator working side by side to lead the organization. The Chief Executive Officer serves as LEDC’s Visionary, focused on idea generation, creative problem solving, and culture. The Chief Operating Officer serves as LEDC’s Integrator, responsible for the operational execution of that vision, holding the leadership team accountable, resolving cross-departmental issues, and ensuring Human Resources, Operations, Finance, and the organization’s evaluation/impact function work in a coordinated way toward shared goals.

Position Summary:
The Chief Operating Officer (COO) is a senior leadership position responsible for the day-to-day operational execution of LEDC’s strategy. Reporting directly to the CEO, the COO oversees Human Resources, Operations, Finance, and the Impact Consultant, translating the CEO's vision and the Board-approved strategic plan into coordinated, accountable execution across departments.

The COO also represents LEDC externally in select capital, funder, and partnership relationships, particularly those tied to financial sustainability and the growth of LEDC’s lending capital base.
 Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

Strategic & Organizational Leadership
Serve as LEDC’s Integrator: run the organization’s leadership team meetings, hold department heads accountable to their priorities and performance metrics, and ensure organization-wide execution stays on track.
Translate the Board-approved strategic plan into department-level goals, and monitor execution against them.
Coordinate with CEO and program directors on staffing, operating costs, budgets, resource allocation, and feasibility of new initiatives.
Support CEO and Chief of Development by providing expertise to external relationships as needed, including maintaining relationships with banks, the CDFI Fund, and impact investors to help raise debt capital and credit facilities that fund LEDC’s loan portfolio.
Build and maintain relationships with relevant government agency partners as needed to support program and funding relationships.

Operations, Finance, & HR Leadership
Refine and design internal operating policies, policies, facilities, and administrative infrastructure to promote efficiency, accountability, and cross-functional collaboration.
Oversee Human Resources, including talent strategy, compensation structure, policies, hiring, and staff performance reviews and development systems. An integral part of overseeing HR will include benefits analysis on a yearly basis.
Oversee Operations, including facilities across LEDC’s DC, Arlington, Baltimore, White Oak offices, IT/systems infrastructure, vendor contracts, and insurance.
Oversee the Finance department’s strategic direction in partnership with the Director of Finance, including budget and audit cadence, without displacing the Director of Finance’s day-to-day leadership of the Finance team.
Oversee work of organizational consultants implementing process and systems improvements (e.g. new database builds, impact evaluation, Traction implementation).

Processes, Systems, & Accountability
Identify and manage organizational risk, including compliance, data security, and operational risk beyond purely financial matters.
Evaluate and pilot new tools (e.g., AI implementation), new processes (e.g. impact evaluation, market analysis, earned revenue), and manage related policy and training.
Own the EOS model implementation across teams: scorecards, rocks, quarterly reviews.

Compliance & Risk Management
Ensure LEDC maintains compliance with the financial covenants tied to its CDFI lending capital raise, working closely with the Director of Lending to structure, monitor, and report on covenant compliance to lenders and investors.
Partner closely with the Director of Lending to ensure LEDC maintains sufficient liquidity to support and grow its loan portfolio, coordinating capital planning between Finance and Lending.
Lead enterprise risk management across the organization: identify, assess, and prioritize strategic, operational, financial, compliance, and reputational risks, and develop mitigation, contingency, and business continuity plans appropriate to LEDC’s size, mission, and risk exposure.
Champion data security, cybersecurity, and privacy practices across the organization, and ensure LEDC carries adequate insurance coverage to protect its people, assets, and mission.
Provide regular risk assessments and updates to the CEO and Board of Directors to support informed governance and oversight.

Specific duties may vary based on program needs, funding requirements, and operational priorities. As the role evolves, additional responsibilities may be assigned.

 5+ years of leadership experience in nonprofit operations, program management, or related field.

Experience with organizational operations, finance, and/or HR management.

Job Description:

Job Summary:
The Executive Director Facilities Engineering & EHS oversees network operations for the Facilities and Environmental Health and Safety (EHS) Departments for JPS Health Network. This role provides direct consultation to the Planning, Design, and Construction (PD&C) department on all construction projects specific to design and construction for Mechanical, Electrical, and Plumbing (MEP) systems and compliance. This role ensures compliance with regulatory standards for building operations, medical equipment management, and healthcare-related codes. This position maintains all JPS network facilities (district-owned, district-leased, and newly built or renovated facilities and property) in compliance with all Authorities Having Jurisdiction (AHJs) to meet and/or exceed regulatory requirements for accreditation. The Executive Director provides leadership direction and support to all stakeholders to ensure compliance with all aspects of the physical environment to include safety, security, hazardous waste and materials, fire safety, medical equipment, and facilities management. This role collaborates with stakeholders to reduce incidents and improve regulatory compliance across all facilities.

Essential Job Functions & Accountabilities

Oversees the near-term and long-term strategic planning for the Facilities and EHS departments relative to JPS Health Network’s strategic, financial, and guality metrics.
Oversees all functional areas of Facilities and EHS for the Main Hospital Campus, Community Health Clinics, JPS Ambulatory Surgery Center, and owned or leased properties including real estate assets.
Develops, implements and manages budgets (operational, capital, and Grant Funds) respective to Facilities Engineering and EHS operations.
Oversees the evaluation and completion of lifecycle costs analysis for all MEP equipment and systems utilized during capital planning.
Partners and consults directly with the PDC department on capital planning budgets for MEP system replacements and upgrades for all construction projects.
Engages in capital construction & renovation projects for JPS relative to design & installation of MEP systems.
Reviews and approves all architectural plans and specifications related to Life Safety and MEP systems to ensure compliance with local, state, and federal code requirements on all construction projects.
Serves as executive leader with direct oversight and responsibility of the programming, design, and construction efforts for the Central Utility Plant as part of JPS’s Master Facilities Plan Program.
Plans and establishes goals through the development of the strategic KPI’s and organizational objectives for the physical environment management plan setting the organization up for success and establishing a strong safety culture.
Oversees compliance and adherence of equipment acquisitions, and equipment dispositions to meet local, state, and federal requirements.
Provides regulatory guidance and consultation to leadership and staff regarding accreditation standards, codes, and requirements, including The Joint Commission, CMS, FGI, IBC, NFPA, ASHRAE, NEC, OSHA, CAP, EPA, TCEQ, DSHS, and other applicable agencies.
Develops and implements “Best Practices” (Standards) for existing on-going maintenance/replacement and future capital investment for all Mechanical, Electrical, and Plumbing systems, and Utilities Management.
